verdict.rationale: Fedora's own docs say you can install desktop apps with one click from Fedora's repositories and Flathub, and can install, update and manage packages, including from the command line. That covers the core of the story: installing apps from an official catalog. Community reports note friction for some proprietary apps (Discord, Spotify needed manual commands, and some apps did not appear in the menu) and general Flatpak papercuts. Those are caveats, not a refutation that the catalog exists. Missing for 10: evidence of catalog scale ("thousands" of apps is never quantified), independent hands-on confirmation that the catalog install works smoothly, and coverage of popular proprietary apps.
